ghana.title: Ghana Discovery Pilot Partnership Concept
ghana.alt: iPurpose Soul · Systems · AI. iPURPOSE × SDSN YOUTH GHANA Ghana Discovery Pilot Partnership Concept An 8-week pilot connecting self-discovery, AI-guided decision support, and verified local pathways into education, employability and entrepreneurship. Proposed: up to 100 SDSN Youth participants Initial pilot fee: waived 8 weeks Prepared for exploratory partnership discussion Renita Hamilton, MPS — Founder & CEO, iPurpose Strategic Leadership · Social Impact · AI-Enabled Human Development

ghana.title: What is iPurpose?
ghana.alt: What is iPurpose? iPurpose helps emerging leaders move from uncertainty to clarity, informed decisions and practical next steps. Soul → Systems → AI Soul Understand your values, strengths, direction and what matters. Systems Turn that understanding into structure: options, pathways, plans and next steps. AI Navigate information and possibilities with practical support. AI supports judgment; it does not replace it. WHO BUILT IT Renita Hamilton, MPS — Founder & CEO Educator, entrepreneur and social-impact leader with more than two decades of experience spanning education, nonprofit leadership, philanthropy, strategic development, consulting and business ownership. A certified general-education teacher and multi-industry entrepreneur, she created iPurpose at the intersection of human development, practical systems and responsible AI. Her experience also includes public leadership, bringing a systems-level understanding of communities, institutions and opportunity.

ghana.title: Why Ghana. Why now.
ghana.alt: Why Ghana. Why now. The demographic need and digital-policy direction are converging. 36.9% of Ghana's projected population is age 15–35. 21.9% average unemployment among people age 15–35 in the first three quarters of 2025. 2025–2035 Ghana National AI Strategy: human capital, education, local relevance and practical AI adoption. The opening for iPurpose is not simply “career matching.” It is helping young adults translate self-knowledge into an actionable next step inside a rapidly changing economy. Identity + Decisions + Local pathways + Follow-through Sources: Ghana Statistical Service (28 Jul 2026); Ghana Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations (24 Apr 2026).

ghana.title: Why SDSN Youth Ghana is the right partner
ghana.alt: Why SDSN Youth Ghana is the right partner The network already combines youth mobilization, universities and practical sustainable-development action. Built-in Ghana network SDSN Youth Ghana is hosted by the University of Ghana, University of Education, Winneba, and Millennium Promise Alliance Ghana. Direct mission fit The network mobilizes young people to contribute practical solutions, with strong alignment to Quality Education, Decent Work and Reduced Inequalities. 2026 employability activity SDSN Youth Ghana joined Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Cameroon and Benin in a three-day “Empowering Youth for Employability” program in May 2026. iPurpose is proposed as a continuation layer: help participants understand themselves translate learning into personalized next steps connect to verified Ghana opportunities continue receiving guidance after a workshop ends Sources: SDSN Youth Ghana; SDSN Youth “Empowering Youth for Employability” workshop; SDSN global networks.

ghana.title: The gap iPurpose is designed to fill
ghana.alt: The gap iPurpose is designed to fill From one-time insight to ongoing navigation. 1 CLARITY What is happening in my life? 2 PURPOSE What strengths, interests and patterns are emerging? 3 COMPASS What should I explore or do next? 4 OPPORTUNITY Which verified Ghana-specific pathways fit? 5 ACTION What did I actually do — and what comes next? The differentiator: iPurpose stays with the participant after the assessment, helping them move from self-understanding to an informed decision and a real next step.

ghana.title: Proposed 8-week iPurpose × SDSN Youth Ghana Pilot
ghana.alt: Proposed 8-week iPurpose × SDSN Youth Ghana Pilot Small enough to learn quickly. Structured enough to produce useful evidence. SDSN Youth cohort: up to 100 participants Ghanaian university students, recent graduates and emerging professionals age 18+ recruited with SDSN Youth Ghana and participating host institutions. Independent Ghana cohort: up to 50 A separate, independently recruited Ghana cohort broadens the learning beyond the SDSN-recruited group. No SDSN recruitment responsibility. Weekly learning loop Usage analytics + short check-ins + selected interviews reveal where language, recommendations, product flow or local context needs adjustment. Week 0 Baseline Consent + clarity measure Weeks 1–2 Activate Clarity + Purpose + Compass Weeks 3–6 Use Guidance + local opportunities Weeks 7–8 Reflect Action + retention + interviews Closeout Report SDSN readout + recommendations

ghana.title: What SDSN Youth Ghana receives
ghana.alt: What SDSN Youth Ghana receives The pilot should create value for participants and useful evidence for the network. Participant access Full pilot access to the iPurpose experience for the agreed SDSN Youth Ghana cohort. Localized pathway layer A Ghana-focused starter library of verified education, career, entrepreneurship and skills opportunities. Pilot analytics Aggregated funnel and engagement measures showing how participants move from onboarding to action. Participant feedback Structured qualitative feedback on usefulness, cultural fit, opportunity navigation and unmet needs. Closeout report A concise readout covering outcomes, lessons and recommendations, including whether and how any wider testing is justified. Co-design influence SDSN Youth Ghana feedback helps shape how iPurpose works for emerging leaders in Ghana. Proposed pilot fee: WAIVED for the initial 8-week evaluation, subject to mutually agreed scope, safeguards and data/compliance requirements.

ghana.title: What we would ask of SDSN Youth Ghana
ghana.alt: What we would ask of SDSN Youth Ghana A deliberately light network lift. 1 Designate one liaison A primary contact for scope, scheduling and coordination with participating institutions. 2 Recruit up to 100 participants Preferably university students, recent graduates and emerging professionals age 18+. 3 Support one orientation A short virtual or hybrid launch session explaining the pilot and participation expectations. 4 Participate in two feedback touchpoints Mid-pilot check-in and end-of-pilot review with relevant SDSN Youth Ghana and institutional representatives. 5 Advise on Ghana relevance Flag missing pathways, terminology, local context or partnership opportunities. Not requested: funding, procurement, exclusivity, endorsement, or a long-term commitment before evidence is available.

ghana.title: How success will be measured
ghana.alt: How success will be measured Downloads are not the goal. Progress from uncertainty toward action is. Activation % completing onboarding Self-discovery Clarity / Purpose completion Compass use Repeat AI-guided navigation Retention Week 2 / 4 / 8 return Opportunity Verified pathway clicks Action Reported real-world next steps Core outcome questions “How clear are you about what you should do next?” “What next step have you decided on or taken?” Clarity measured at entry and again at closeout; decisions and actions tracked through the pilot.

ghana.title: Guardrails: participant support, privacy and trust
ghana.alt: Guardrails: participant support, privacy and trust The pilot must be useful without blurring the line between AI guidance and professional services. Decision support — not counseling iPurpose will not be positioned as a mental-health service, diagnostic tool, or replacement for professional counseling or career services. Verified local opportunities For Ghana-specific programs and opportunities, verified sources should take priority over model memory; uncertain information is clearly labeled. 18+ initial cohort The initial pilot is limited to adults age 18+ while the model, safeguards and participation experience are evaluated. Data minimization Collect only what is needed for the experience and pilot evaluation; clearly state purpose, retention and deletion choices. Aggregated reporting SDSN receives cohort-level findings; individual participant content is not included in routine network reporting. Compliance review before launch Cross-border processing, consent, controller responsibilities and Ghana data-protection requirements are confirmed before recruitment.

ghana.title: A 90-day path to launch, and the ask
ghana.alt: A 90-day path to launch, and the ask The first conversation does not need to solve the entire partnership. 01 SCOPING 30-minute discussion Confirm fit, cohort + liaison 02 PREPARE Localize context Verify opportunities Compliance review 03 RECRUIT SDSN/partner recruitment Participant consent Orientation 04 PILOT 8 weeks of use Check-ins + analytics User interviews 05 DECIDE Closeout report Expand / revise / stop No automatic commitment Would SDSN Youth Ghana be open to exploring an 8-week iPurpose pilot with up to 100 Ghanaian emerging leaders, potentially in collaboration with one or more host institutions? If there is mutual fit, we would jointly refine the cohort, safeguards, local opportunity layer and evaluation plan before recruitment begins. The work matters for Ghana in its own right, whatever comes next. A 30-minute exploratory conversation. No long-term commitment. Primary outreach: Johnnie Kojo Hayford, Network Coordinator, SDSN Youth Ghana. The University of Ghana is one of SDSN Youth Ghana's host institutions. Contact Renita: renita@ipurposesoul.com | SDSN Youth Ghana: Johnnie.hayford@sdsnyouth.org · ghana@sdsnyouth.org | SDSN Youth partnership: youth@unsdsn.org
